sources.entry: llama.cpp — High-performance local inference engine for LLMs and multimodal models, supporting CPU/GPU execution, quantization, and broad model compatibility.
llama.cpp - Where new quantization types, kernels and thread pools land first, each with the perplexity and speed table behind it.

summary.one_liner: llama.cpp is a C/C++ inference engine for running LLMs and vision-language models locally or in the cloud across CPUs and many GPU backends.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes llama.cpp as a plain C/C++ implementation (no dependencies) built on the ggml library, aimed at LLM and VLM inference with minimal setup. It lists support for 1.5- to 8-bit integer quantization, SIMD paths for x86 (AVX/AVX2/AVX512/AMX), ARM NEON and Apple Metal/Accelerate, and RISC-V vector extensions. GPU backends named include CUDA, HIP (AMD), MUSA (Moore Threads), Vulkan, SYCL, Metal, OpenCL, WebGPU and others, and CPU+GPU hybrid inference is supported for models larger than VRAM. The README also shows a `llama cli` tool and a `llama serve` command that exposes an OpenAI-compatible API server with a built-in web UI, plus GBNF grammar support and a llama-server REST API.
use_cases: run LLMs locally on a laptop or desktop
serve an OpenAI-compatible chat API on local hardware
run quantized models on limited memory
multimodal (vision-language) inference from the command line
partial GPU offload for models bigger than VRAM
inference on Apple silicon, NVIDIA, AMD or Intel hardware
how_to_run: Download pre-built binaries from the releases page
Build from source by cloning the repository (see build guide)
notable: Plain C/C++ with no external dependencies, built on the ggml library
Broad backend coverage from CUDA, HIP and Metal to Vulkan, SYCL, WebGPU and CANN (Ascend NPU)
Built-in web UI and OpenAI-compatible llama-server
Hybrid CPU+GPU inference for models larger than VRAM
caveats: Some backends are marked as in progress (e.g., OpenVINO), so support may be incomplete
Hardware-specific builds and backends need separate setup, as described in the build docs
The README does not give detailed platform or performance numbers
